chapter: Image, travel and Black, Brown and Beige
title: Freddie Guy, the steady guitarist
summary: Greer calls Freddie Guy the sensible rock of the band, who just kept time.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: I gave you one, didn't I?
Yeah, I've got it right here. But what I had wanted to ask you about, the -- one of the people who very rarely gets talked about is Freddy Guy.

Yeah. You see, Duke and Freddy was -- he was a beautiful guy. And Freddy, out of the whole aggregation, whole band, Freddy was the sensible one. He didn't have no wild traits like the musicians, like us. He was a rock of Gibraltar, steady. And all he had to do was keep that time, on that guitar. That's all. The four fingers you were talking about, that was his job. There's no record or recollection of him playing the guitar like the solo guys play, now, All he had to do was play tempo. And he was like the Rock of Gibraltar. That was his job.

And he was the mainstay of the band, rock steady. That's right. He was a lady's man. Nice looking guy, lady's man. Him and Sweetie Brown, lady's men. But Duke, Duke would always -- he was with the guys night and day. That's right.
